title: Slice S: --stream on callers, impact and code-map (DEC-299, command contract 1a)
description: glyph 0.1.0 ships with streaming (DEC-299, operator first-party 'Streaming in 0.1.0'). Implements section 1a of opum-doc docs/specs/opum-command-contract.md (opum-ai/opum-doc#1914) for callers, impact and code-map. diff is OUT of scope. Independent of Slice P. Floor work (public surface): Opus review before landing.

acceptanceCriteria.text: callers, impact and code-map each declare --stream in the help --json manifest (proof: a manifest test asserts the flag on exactly those three commands and on no other, diff included)
--stream on a command that does not declare it (diff and every other undeclared command) exits 2 (proof: a test per undeclared command asserts exit 2 and the usage error envelope on stderr)
--stream combined with --plain exits 2 (proof: test on each of the three commands)

--stream stdout is NDJSON: every line parses as a section 2 envelope, is compact, newline-terminated, has no blank lines, carries principal as the last top-level key, and is flushed when written (proof: conformance test parses every stdout line; flush proved by reading a pipe incrementally and observing an item line before the process exits)

the last line carries the command result kind (callers.result, impact.result, code-map.result) and its data is the batch answer data with the item list replaced by itemCount; earlier lines are <command>.item with one list element each (proof: test asserts last-line kind, itemCount equals the item line count, and every non-item field equals the batch result)

for the same inputs the multiset of item data values equals the non-stream answer item list, for each of the three commands (proof: test compares sorted multisets against the batch --json output on a fixture repo)

a forced mid-stream failure leaves no result line on stdout, writes the section 5 error envelope to stderr and exits with the mapped non-zero code (proof: test injects a failure after at least one item line for each command and asserts all three clauses)

code-map keeps ADR 0005 wall-time budget under --stream and its result line states whether the budget truncated it (proof: test with a tiny budget asserts truncated true and a test with a generous budget asserts truncated false, both on the result line)
invocations without --stream are byte-for-byte unchanged (proof: existing batch tests pass unmodified, and a golden comparison of batch --json output before and after on the fixture repo)
a component ADR in docs/ names DEC-299, records the stream design as implemented, and lore check exits 0 (proof: lore check at the pinned lore version)
README documents --stream for the three commands (proof: README section present and its example output matches a test fixture)
